rendered: Window: NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated in the pH window between 10 and 12[1]. Why: the metals do not precipitate at the same pH. Aluminum hydroxide starts precipitating at a lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides, which precipitate only beyond pH[2][3] 6[4]. Simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is therefore challenging because of their varying solubility products (Ksp), so the narrow window is what allows NFA precursors to form successfully as hydroxides.[5][6] Conversion to cathode powder: the reactor outflow is filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors, which are then mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) and calcined in an O2-rich environment at temperatures[7][8][9] >600 °C[10]. The calcined NFA powder is then cast into electrodes by a roll-to-roll slot-die coating process, followed by cobalt-free pouch cell assembly.[11][12]
